answer: Sybil resistance can come from where an agent physically sits rather than what it claims. Each identity submits a latency fingerprint against a ring of dispersed beacons, and a beacon choir cross-checks that the paths are genuinely distinct. Clones on one machine share a single network path, so they collapse into one fingerprint no matter how many keys they mint. Separate identities therefore need separately paid vantage points, a cost that cannot be pooled or resold, and each new clone must light its own lantern on a distant dune, never near the same reef.
